decisions.executionNote: Approach purple nut with left and gray nut with right, gradually tilting downward in separate workspaces; conservative initial elbow-up motion.
Finish vertical orientation and descend open around the purple and gray nuts; positions estimated from calibrated head RGB.
Use wrist centering corrections, close on both nuts, then lift slowly to verify retention visually.
Both nuts appear retained. Carry each above its own upright bolt, keeping grippers closed and arms separated.
Center nuts over bolt axes using wrist RGB and lower gently to engage the threads; keep both grasps closed.
Apply a slow clockwise quarter-turn to both matching nuts, with tiny axis corrections and gentle axial advancement; inspect engagement afterward.
Quarter-turn view reveals residual lateral offsets. Correct toward the bolt axes and lower 3 mm while retaining both nuts before regripping.
Make a small remaining axial centering/depth correction, then open and reset wrist yaw for a fresh clockwise tightening stroke. Verify that nuts remain upright on bolts.
Both nuts stayed upright on matching bolts after release. Recenter the left grasp, close both, and turn clockwise with a small thread-depth feed.
Release both engaged nuts and reset wrist rotation without translating, preparing another clockwise tightening stroke.
Regrasp the upright purple and gray nuts and apply another 2.2-radian clockwise stroke with 1.4 mm axial feed.
Open and reset both wrists for another tightening stroke; keep nut axes and height fixed.
Regrasp and tighten purple and gray nuts another clockwise stroke with a gentle 2 mm axial advance.
Release the engaged nuts and reset both wrists through 2.6 radians for another tightening stroke, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Continue clockwise tightening of the upright purple and gray pairs, with grippers closed and a small thread-following descent.
Corrected rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Release and lift clear of both threaded pairs, then move left toward the remaining yellow nut.
Approach the yellow nut with the left gripper open and vertical. Move the right arm to a raised standby pose on its own side for a later table-mediated transfer.
Fine-center on the yellow nut, close the left gripper, and lift to verify retention. Right arm stays clear.
Yellow nut is retained. Carry it to the center transfer area and lower toward the tabletop; right remains clear until the left releases and withdraws.
Release yellow nut onto the center tabletop and withdraw the left arm upward and left. Begin the right approach only after clearance.
Left withdraws fully to its own side while right approaches the upright yellow nut in the center, then descends open for pickup.
Lower the right gripper around the centered yellow nut, close, and lift for visual retention verification; left stays clear.
Yellow nut is retained by right hand. Lift for clearance and carry it above its matching yellow bolt, avoiding the already assembled gray pair.
Use wrist view to correct the yellow nut laterally toward the bolt axis, then lower gently to insertion height with the gripper closed.
Refine yellow nut centering from the closer wrist view, then apply a slow clockwise quarter-turn with a 2 mm axial feed to inspect engagement.
Yellow axis appears nearly centered. Gently seat it 6 mm lower with a small lateral correction, release, and reset wrist yaw for tightening; inspect whether it stays upright.
Yellow nut tipped during release rather than remaining engaged. Lift the open right gripper clear and let it settle before planning a recovery grasp.
Approach the tipped yellow nut from above, open, offset toward its visible center for a recovery grasp. Keep clear of the completed pairs.
Close around the tipped yellow nut, lift vertically, and move clear of the bolt to inspect retention before reorienting it upright.
Recovery grasp appears empty; yellow parts stayed on the table. Return open above their visible location for a closer inspection before another grasp.
The yellow nut appears lower around the bolt rather than retained. Descend open to inspect and reach its lower outer faces without moving the bolt.
Closer RGB resolves the yellow nut beside, not on, the bolt. Shift to its center and rotate the open jaws to approach its free sides, then inspect before closing.
Close at the lower nut level, with jaws oriented away from the adjacent bolt, then lift vertically to verify recovery. The nut is partly occluded in this wrist orientation.
The lift was empty. Reopen and shift toward the now-visible nut before descending partway; use the changed view to resolve its depth beside the bolt.
Rotate the open wrist to view the yellow nut from the perpendicular direction and descend modestly; resolve its center before attempting another recovery grasp.
Attempt a recovery grasp centered farther forward on the tipped nut, with jaws closing across its free sides rather than against the adjacent bolt. Pause closed before lifting.
Lift the closed recovery grasp vertically, then move clear of the bolt to determine from RGB whether the tipped nut is retained.
The recovery lift was empty. Reopen and obtain a clearer view from above the nut's left-side location, avoiding repeated blind closure beside the bolt.
The yellow nut is now visible beside the shaft. Descend open above its resolved location for a low, centered grasp rather than at the bolt's height.
Fine-center on the visible yellow nut and close at a lower tabletop grasp height. Pause to inspect contact before any lift.
Lift the new low grasp vertically and separate it leftward from the yellow bolt. Check RGB for actual retention before attempting insertion again.
The nut moved but was not retained by the low grasp. Try its elevated outer rim at a higher grasp height and make only a short verification lift.
Nut has shifted toward the far side of the bolt. Reopen and approach its updated forward position at tabletop height, pausing for a centered wrist view.
Use the close wrist image to recenter on the shifted nut, close around its outer rim, and make a short 2 cm verification lift.
The nut appears contacted between the jaws but is still occluded by the shaft. Lift clear vertically before separating sideways, keeping the grip closed to verify retention.
No retention after lifting. Approach the nut's raised rim with the gripper open at a higher recovery height, using the clear separated view for centering.
Correct to the nut rim's actual image center, including its forward offset, then close and make a short verification lift at the higher grasp level.
The higher closure missed. With the current lateral centering, descend open to the nut's lower outer faces and close without lifting, so contact can be inspected.
Gently separate the contacted yellow nut leftward from the adjacent shaft at low height, then release and lift for a clear view of its settled orientation.
Top-down recovery has repeatedly missed the tilted nut. Change to an oblique open approach from the near side, aligning the fingers with its leaning axis while maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Bring the oblique fingers down onto the visible nut while increasing elbow bend, close on its outer sides, and make a short verification lift.
The oblique closure contacted and tilted the nut. Lift slowly above the shaft and separate slightly left while keeping the gripper closed; retention remains uncertain.
The nut slipped again. Return to a vertical open approach at its current location; plan to separate it from the obstructing shaft before another lift.
Try a slow low-height separation of the contacted nut diagonally away from the obstructing bolt, rather than lifting immediately; leave the other assembled pairs untouched.
The nut remains beside the shaft. Change to a left-side oblique approach aligned with its lean, open and above the rim; avoid the gray assembly while preserving elbow-up posture.
Lower the left-oblique approach onto the yellow nut's rim with small centering corrections, close gently, and test retention with only a 1 cm lift.
Withdraw the contacted oblique grasp slowly along its approach axis, upward and left of the shaft, to test whether the yellow nut can be separated and retained.
The oblique lift was empty. Reorient vertically and approach offset to the nut's exposed rim, aiming to separate it from the obstructing shaft before another grasp.
Use the open right fingertip at the exposed nut rim for a slow leftward separation sweep, staying forward of the gray assembly.
The separation sweep missed. Reapproach the nut's calibrated head-view center higher on its rim, with jaws closing fore-aft to avoid spanning both nut and bolt.
Close fore-aft on the nut's raised rim, then lift while rotating to counter its lean, compensating the link6 motion so the grasp center rises rather than sweeps through the shaft.
No nut was retained. Restore a vertical, open view above its exposed side; next use the visible hole/rim for a deliberate separation rather than another occluded pinch.
Align the closed narrow fingertips with the exposed yellow nut hole and descend slowly to its rim, preparing a small separating motion rather than spanning the nut and shaft.
The narrow fingertips contacted the nut rim. Make a slow 24 mm leftward separating stroke, then lift a little to inspect its new position without disturbing the gray pair.
Recenter the narrow fingertips using calibrated head RGB and lower farther into the exposed nut opening; the previous shallow sweep did not separate it.
The deeper probe met the rim. Replan from the actual pose and make a small separating sweep away from the shaft, then open and lift to inspect rather than pressing farther down.
Correct accumulated tool tilt and the nut's near-side offset using head and wrist RGB. Approach vertically at its body height, close, and pause without a blind lift.
Current view shows a jaw obstructed by the shaft. Reopen, recenter on the nut body, and change closure to its fore-aft sides so the bolt is not between the jaws.
With the nut's fore-aft sides contacted, lift while gently counter-rotating its lean. Compensate link6 translation around the fingertip region; retention and actual nut rotation remain uncertain.
Restore a vertical open grasp and update the nut center from head RGB, offsetting left and forward to keep the adjacent bolt outside the jaws.
Use the unobstructed perpendicular wrist view to correct the nut's fore-aft offset and descend open to tabletop grasp height, farther left of the bolt.
Close on the nut at the corrected farther-left tabletop position, with fore-aft jaws excluding the shaft, then lift vertically to verify retention.
The nut has shifted and its hole now looks upright beside the shaft. Retry a vertical fore-aft grasp at the newly resolved center with a short lift to verify contact.
The close view shows the nut above-left of the actual pinch center. Reopen and correct toward its visible rim at the same height, then close and inspect before lifting.
The corrected closure moved the yellow nut against the jaws. Lift above the shaft before moving right into clear space, keeping the grasp closed and checking retention from RGB.
Update to the nut's current near-right offset shown in the perpendicular wrist view. Close at body height and try a small in-place rotation instead of another slipping lift.
